help.dues-projections.title: Dues Projections
help.dues-projections.summary: What the family should collect this year, what has come in, and who still owes.
help.dues-projections.what-it-is.heading: What it answers
help.dues-projections.what-it-is.b0: [Transactions](/accounting/transactions) is what came in. This is what should: every active dues schedule, multiplied out across the members who owe it, set against what has actually been collected.
help.dues-projections.what-it-is.b1: Nothing on this screen changes anything. Recording a payment or waiving one is on [Transactions](/accounting/transactions); changing what a due costs is under [Accounting](/admin/accounting).
help.dues-projections.what-it-is.b2: **A relative who has died is not counted.** Setting a **Sunset Date** on somebody’s profile takes them off this screen entirely — they owe nothing, so neither the total the family is owed nor the list of who has still to pay includes them. Payments they made in the past still count toward what was collected.
help.dues-projections.figures.heading: The four figures
help.dues-projections.figures.b0.i0.text: What the members counted here owe for their schedules' current periods. Everything else on the screen is a fraction of it.
help.dues-projections.figures.b0.i1.text: Money that actually arrived. A reversal nets itself out, so a corrected payment leaves the figure where it belongs.
help.dues-projections.figures.b0.i2.text: Forgiven. It settles the due and comes off what is still owed — and it is never counted as money, because none arrived.
help.dues-projections.figures.b0.i3.text: Expected, less what has been settled either way. The number the screen exists for.
help.dues-projections.figures.b1: A fifth appears only when there is any: money **awaiting settlement**, which is a payment started and not yet confirmed. It is not counted as collected and has not been taken off what is owed.
help.dues-projections.year.heading: Which year
help.dues-projections.year.b0: Each schedule's own. A due anchored on 1 April and a levy anchored on 1 January genuinely have two years in progress, so every row states the period it was measured over and the family total is the sum of them.
help.dues-projections.year.b1: This is why the totals here agree with what each member sees on their own [Dues](/accounting/dues-and-donations) screen. A single calendar year would have been tidier and would have disagreed with every member's balance.
help.dues-projections.who-is-counted.b0: Everybody the family has approved — the same list the [Member Directory](/community/directory) shows. Somebody recorded on the [family tree](/community/family-tree) who has never signed in owes their dues exactly as much as anybody else does, so they are counted. Leaving them out never made the debt smaller; it made this screen report a smaller one.
help.dues-projections.who-is-counted.b1: The **Status** column answers a different question from the money: whether there is anybody to send an invoice to.
They have an account, and the due shows on their own [Dues](/accounting/dues-and-donations) screen.
No account yet, and an invitation is still open. The family has asked, and the ball is with them.
Recorded in the family and never asked to join. This is the one of the three you can act on — invite them from the [family tree](/community/family-tree).
help.dues-projections.who-is-counted.b3: An invitation that has **expired** reads as Pending Invite rather than Invited. An expired link cannot be accepted, so the family has to ask again, and saying otherwise would report work as done.
help.dues-projections.who-is-counted.b4: **Still to collect** says underneath it how much of itself is owed by people with no account. That is part of the total and never a deduction from it: the family is owed the money whether or not there is an inbox to send the bill to.
help.dues-projections.who-is-counted.b5: Five things reduce what somebody owes, and all five are honoured: a due that starts at an age, a due only the bloodline owes, a due for one region or chapter, an optional due they have declined, and anything the family has waived.
help.dues-projections.who-is-counted.b6: Anyone with no date of birth recorded owes an age-limited due in full, because an age is never guessed at. If a figure looks too high, that is the first thing to check.
help.dues-projections.who-is-counted.b7: Somebody still waiting to be approved is **not** counted. They have not joined the family yet, so nothing is owed by them.
help.dues-projections.standings.heading: Where each member stands
help.dues-projections.standings.b0: The member table leads with the people to chase. A row reports the **least** settled standing that member holds on any schedule, so somebody paid up on three dues and owing a fourth is listed as owing.
help.dues-projections.standings.b1.i0.te: Owes the whole amount for this period.
help.dues-projections.standings.b1.i1.te: Something in, not all of it.
help.dues-projections.standings.b1.i3.te: Opted out of an optional due.
help.dues-projections.standings.b1.i4.te: Below the age that due starts at. Not the same as settled — they have paid nothing and owe nothing.
help.dues-projections.standings.b1.i5.te: The due is restricted to the bloodline and this member is outside it. Unlike "Not yet due", it will never become theirs.
help.dues-projections.standings.b1.i6.te: The due is for one region or chapter and they are in another — or in none, which puts them under National. Unlike "Not theirs", this one changes if they change chapter.
help.dues-projections.standings.b2: **Standing** and **Status** are two different columns, and the row worth looking at is one that is both Nothing paid and Pending Invite. Standing is about the money; Status is about whether anybody can be asked for it.
help.dues-projections.standings.b3: A bloodline-only due on a family that has not named its line is owed by nobody, and its row says so rather than showing an unexplained $0.00 expected.
help.dues-projections.standings.b4: **Only those who owe** narrows the table, and the filter box searches any part of any name.
